cosy-lesson.title: What's the Point of YouTube Auto-Launching Shorts?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Algorithmic feed ≠ Curated selection – an automated stream of content chosen by software rules ≠ a thoughtfully chosen collection of materials.

p.em: Example: An algorithmic feed prioritizes engagement over quality, unlike a curated selection chosen by human editors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Short-form video ≠ Long-form documentary – brief video content under sixty seconds ≠ extended, in-depth cinematic non-fiction work.

p.em: Example: Binging short-form video clips leaves little room for the deep storytelling found in a long-form documentary.

cosy-blockquote.p: Instant gratification ≠ Delayed reward – immediate fulfillment of a desire without waiting ≠ satisfaction gained through patience and effort.

p.em: Example: App notifications deliver instant gratification, whereas mastering a complex musical instrument offers a delayed reward.

cosy-blockquote.p: Auto-launch ≠ Manual playback – the automatic starting of media upon opening an app ≠ initiating video playback by conscious choice.

p.em: Example: The auto-launch update forces media upon users, whereas manual playback respects individual user initiative.

cosy-blockquote.p: Passive scrolling ≠ Intentional viewing – mindlessly swiping through media feeds without a goal ≠ actively selecting specific content to watch.

p.em: Example: Passive scrolling often leads to screen fatigue, while intentional viewing helps us absorb valuable information.

cosy-blockquote.p: Attention span ≠ Prolonged focus – the length of time a person can concentrate on a subject ≠ sustained, deep concentration over an extended period.

p.em: Example: A short attention span makes reading thick books challenging, requiring practice to restore prolonged focus.

cosy-blockquote.p: Frictionless consumption ≠ Mindful engagement – effortless absorbing of digital media without obstacles ≠ conscious, reflective participation with content.

p.em: Example: Tech companies design for frictionless consumption, making mindful engagement harder to maintain.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dopamine loop ≠ Calming reflection – a continuous neurochemical cycle seeking novel stimuli ≠ a peaceful mental state of quiet contemplation.

p.em: Example: Swiping endless video reels creates a dopamine loop that prevents calming reflection before sleep.

cosy-blockquote.p: User retention ≠ Conscious exit – a platform's metric for keeping users active on the app ≠ deliberately closing an application when finished.

p.em: Example: Features engineered for user retention actively work against a user's attempt at a conscious exit.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hyper-stimulation ≠ Sensory rest – overwhelming the senses with fast-paced digital input ≠ allowing sensory organs and mind to relax without screens.

p.em: Example: Late-night hyper-stimulation from bright, noisy phone clips robs the mind of essential sensory rest.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Does an automated algorithmic feed ≠ curated selection deprive us of the power to decide what we want to consume?
★ When an app automatically feeds you content, do you usually watch it or try to close it?

Why has short-form video ≠ long-form documentary become the default media format across major social networks?
★ How often do you watch long documentaries compared to short vertical reels?

How does constant exposure to instant gratification ≠ delayed reward affect our willingness to read books or master complex skills?
★ Do you find it harder to stay focused on a long book or film than you did five years ago?

Is the trend toward auto-launch ≠ manual playback an aggressive intrusion into user intention?
★ Have you ever muted your phone specifically to avoid unexpected auto-playing audio?

Why does passive scrolling ≠ intentional viewing leave users feeling exhausted rather than refreshed?
★ Have you ever closed a social media app after 30 minutes and realized you remember nothing you saw?

Is our collective attention span ≠ prolonged focus shrinking permanently due to fast-paced mobile updates?
★ What is one activity where you still enjoy uninterrupted, deep concentration?

Why do app designers prioritize frictionless consumption ≠ mindful engagement at the expense of user choice?
★ Do you feel tech companies should add optional 'friction' to help users limit screen time?

How dangerous is entering an endless dopamine loop ≠ calming reflection right before bedtime?
★ Do you keep your phone near your bed when you go to sleep?

Does prioritizing corporate user retention ≠ conscious exit make technology feel more like a trap than a tool?
★ Have you ever uninstalled an application because it was taking up too much of your time?

What are the psychological costs of constant digital hyper-stimulation ≠ sensory rest during our free moments?
★ What do you usually do when waiting in a line-look at your phone or observe your surroundings?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: - 🔍Opening an app with a clear purpose and initiating manual playback - 📲Letting auto-launch feeds take over and surfing algorithmic recommendations

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Auto-launching short videos immediately upon opening an app prioritizes algorithmic feed ≠ curated selection mechanics over genuine human curiosity.
★ Do you feel annoyed when an application decides what you watch before you search?

The dominance of short-form video ≠ long-form documentary formats is re-wiring human cognitive habits to reject slow-paced, detailed arguments.
★ Do you think fast-paced video clips make people less patient in real-life conversations?

Society's addiction to instant gratification ≠ delayed reward is degrading our ability to complete long-term projects and personal goals.
★ Is there a long-term goal you achieved recently that required months of patient effort?

Regulators should mandate that auto-launch ≠ manual playback features be turned off by default to protect consumer mental well-being.
★ Would you support a law requiring tech platforms to ask permission before auto-playing content?

Replacing active research with passive scrolling ≠ intentional viewing is turning modern internet users from creators into passive consumers.
★ Do you consider yourself more of a content creator or a content consumer?

A reduced average attention span ≠ prolonged focus among younger generations will force schools and workplaces to drastically simplify communication.
★ Have you noticed presentation styles at work or school getting shorter and punchier?

Designing apps purely for frictionless consumption ≠ mindful engagement strips technology of its original empowering utility.
★ Do you feel smartphones today empower us more or distract us more?

The engineering of an addictive dopamine loop ≠ calming reflection should be treated with the same health warnings as gambling or smoking.
★ Should social media apps carry mental health warning labels on their login screens?

When app metrics prioritize user retention ≠ conscious exit, technology ceases to serve human autonomy and begins serving corporate profit.
★ How do you feel when you realize an app was designed specifically to keep you from closing it?

Without mandatory digital balance and hyper-stimulation ≠ sensory rest, future societies will suffer widespread burnout and chronic anxiety.
★ What is your favorite way to give your mind complete rest from screens and noise?
